claim: Serine palmitoyl transferase (SPT) is the rate-limiting enzyme in the de novo synthesis of sphingolipids (SL).
source: Serine palmitoyl transferase (SPT), the rate-limiting enzyme in the de novo synthesis of sphingolipids (SL), is needed for embryonic development, physiological homeostasis, and response to stress.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in sphingolipid biochemistry, supported by the manuscript's introduction and cited literature.

claim: SPT is needed for embryonic development, physiological homeostasis, and response to stress.
source: Serine palmitoyl transferase (SPT), the rate-limiting enzyme in the de novo synthesis of sphingolipids (SL), is needed for embryonic development, physiological homeostasis, and response to stress.
evidence: This statement is supported by the manuscript's introduction and references to prior research.

claim: Mice with endothelial-specific knockout of SPTLC1 (Sptlc1 ECKO) exhibited reduced EC proliferation.
source: Mice with an endothelial-specific gene knockout of SPTLC1 (Sptlc1 ECKO), an essential subunit of the SPT complex, exhibited reduced EC proliferation and tip/stalk cell differentiation, resulting in delayed retinal vascular development.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F and G, demonstrating reduced phospho-histone H3 positive cells in Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: Mice with endothelial-specific knockout of SPTLC1 (Sptlc1 ECKO) exhibited reduced tip/stalk cell differentiation.
source: Mice with an endothelial-specific gene knockout of SPTLC1 (Sptlc1 ECKO), an essential subunit of the SPT complex, exhibited reduced EC proliferation and tip/stalk cell differentiation, resulting in delayed retinal vascular development.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F and H, demonstrating reduced ESM1+ tip cells in Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: Sptlc1 ECKO mice showed delayed retinal vascular development.
source: Mice with an endothelial-specific gene knockout of SPTLC1 (Sptlc1 ECKO), an essential subunit of the SPT complex, exhibited reduced EC proliferation and tip/stalk cell differentiation, resulting in delayed retinal vascular development.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A-C, demonstrating lower retinal vascular density and delayed radial expansion in Sptlc1 ECKO mice at P6.

claim: Sptlc1 ECKO mice had reduced retinal neovascularization in the oxygen-induced retinopathy model.
source: In addition, Sptlc1 ECKO mice had reduced retinal neovascularization in the oxygen-induced retinopathy model.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4I and J, demonstrating reduced pathological neovascularization in Sptlc1 ECKO mice at P17.

claim: EC SL produced from the de novo pathway are needed for lipid raft formation.
source: Mechanistic studies suggest that EC SL produced from the de novo pathway are needed for lipid raft formation and efficient VEGF signaling.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F and G, demonstrating that Myriocin treatment reduces lipid raft formation, which can be rescued by dhSph and Sph supplementation.

claim: EC SL produced from the de novo pathway are needed for efficient VEGF signaling.
source: Mechanistic studies suggest that EC SL produced from the de novo pathway are needed for lipid raft formation and efficient VEGF signaling.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and E, demonstrating that Myriocin treatment reduces VEGF-induced ERK phosphorylation, which can be rescued by SL supplementation.

claim: Post-natal deletion of EC Sptlc1 showed rapid reduction of several SL metabolites in plasma.
source: Post-natal deletion of the EC Sptlc1 also showed rapid reduction of several SL metabolites in plasma, red blood cells, and peripheral organs (lung and liver) but not in the retina, part of the central nervous system (CNS).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A-E and Figure 7A, demonstrating reduced SL metabolites in plasma of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: Post-natal deletion of EC Sptlc1 showed rapid reduction of several SL metabolites in red blood cells.
source: Post-natal deletion of the EC Sptlc1 also showed rapid reduction of several SL metabolites in plasma, red blood cells, and peripheral organs (lung and liver) but not in the retina, part of the central nervous system (CNS).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6F-J and Figure 7B, demonstrating reduced SL metabolites in RBC of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: Post-natal deletion of EC Sptlc1 showed rapid reduction of several SL metabolites in peripheral organs (lung and liver).
source: Post-natal deletion of the EC Sptlc1 also showed rapid reduction of several SL metabolites in plasma, red blood cells, and peripheral organs (lung and liver) but not in the retina, part of the central nervous system (CNS).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A-F, demonstrating reduced SL metabolites in lung and liver of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: Post-natal deletion of EC Sptlc1 did not reduce SL metabolites in the retina.
source: Post-natal deletion of the EC Sptlc1 also showed rapid reduction of several SL metabolites in plasma, red blood cells, and peripheral organs (lung and liver) but not in the retina, part of the central nervous system (CNS).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8G-I, demonstrating no change in SL metabolites in retina of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: EC de novo SL synthesis was important for acetaminophen-induced rapid ceramide elevation in the liver.
source: In the liver, EC de novo SL synthesis was important for acetaminophen-induced rapid ceramide elevation and hepatotoxicity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9D-G, demonstrating reduced ceramide elevation in Sptlc1 ECKO liver at 8 hr after APAP treatment.

claim: EC de novo SL synthesis was important for acetaminophen-induced hepatotoxicity.
source: In the liver, EC de novo SL synthesis was important for acetaminophen-induced rapid ceramide elevation and hepatotoxicity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A-C, demonstrating reduced liver injury in Sptlc1 ECKO mice after APAP treatment.

claim: EC-derived SL metabolites are in constant flux between the vasculature, circulatory elements, and parenchymal cells of non-CNS organs.
source: These results suggest that EC-derived SL metabolites are in constant flux between the vasculature, circulatory elements, and parenchymal cells of non-CNS organs.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing reduced SL metabolites in plasma, RBC, lung, and liver but not retina in Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: Endothelial SL biosynthesis plays a central role in maintaining vascular development.
source: Taken together, our data point to the central role of the endothelial SL biosynthesis in maintaining vascular development, neovascular proliferation, non-CNS tissue metabolic homeostasis, and hepatocyte response to stress.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing delayed retinal vascular development in Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: Endothelial SL biosynthesis plays a central role in maintaining neovascular proliferation.
source: Taken together, our data point to the central role of the endothelial SL biosynthesis in maintaining vascular development, neovascular proliferation, non-CNS tissue metabolic homeostasis, and hepatocyte response to stress.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing reduced pathological neovascularization in Sptlc1 ECKO mice in the OIR model.

claim: Endothelial SL biosynthesis plays a central role in maintaining non-CNS tissue metabolic homeostasis.
source: Taken together, our data point to the central role of the endothelial SL biosynthesis in maintaining vascular development, neovascular proliferation, non-CNS tissue metabolic homeostasis, and hepatocyte response to stress.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing reduced SL metabolites in lung and liver of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: Endothelial SL biosynthesis plays a central role in hepatocyte response to stress.
source: Taken together, our data point to the central role of the endothelial SL biosynthesis in maintaining vascular development, neovascular proliferation, non-CNS tissue metabolic homeostasis, and hepatocyte response to stress.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing reduced APAP-induced hepatotoxicity in Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: Complex membrane SL, sphingomyelin (SM) and glycosphingolipids, are enriched in lipid rafts and caveolae.
source: Complex membrane SL, sphingomyelin (SM) and glycosphingolipids, are enriched in lipid rafts and caveolae, which provide an optimal platform for intracellular signaling and cell-cell interactions (van Meer et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in cell biology, supported by the cited reference.

claim: Lipid rafts and caveolae provide an optimal platform for intracellular signaling and cell-cell interactions.

claim: Sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) acts as a ligand for G-protein coupled receptors (S1PR1-5).
source: In contrast, the secreted SL, sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P), acts as a ligand for G-protein coupled receptors (S1PR1-5) which regulate many physiological and pathological functions (Proia and Hla, 2015).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in sphingolipid signaling, supported by the cited reference.

claim: S1P receptors regulate many physiological and pathological functions.

claim: Most cellular SL are synthesized via the de novo pathway.
source: While SL can be derived from dietary sources, most cellular SL are synthesized via the de novo pathway.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in sphingolipid metabolism.

claim: The de novo SL biosynthetic pathway is initiated in the endoplasmic reticulum by the condensation of serine and fatty acyl-CoA to generate 3-ketosphinganine by the serine palmitoyltransferase (SPT) enzyme complex.
source: This pathway is initiated in the endoplasmic reticulum by the condensation of serine and fatty acyl-CoA to generate 3-ketosphinganine by the serine palmitoyltransferase (SPT) enzyme complex.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in sphingolipid biochemistry.

claim: 3-ketosphinganine is converted into dihydrosphingosine (dhSph), dihydroceramide (dhCer), and ultimately ceramide (Cer).
source: The product, 3-ketosphinganine, is further converted into dihydrosphingosine (dhSph), dihydroceramide (dhCer), and ultimately ceramide (Cer), which is a substrate for the production of complex SL and metabolites such as sphingosine (Sph) and S1P (Merrill, 2002).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in sphingolipid biochemistry, supported by the cited reference.

claim: Ceramide is a substrate for the production of complex SL and metabolites such as sphingosine (Sph) and S1P.
source: The product, 3-ketosphinganine, is further converted into dihydrosphingosine (dhSph), dihydroceramide (dhCer), and ultimately ceramide (Cer), which is a substrate for the production of complex SL and metabolites such as sphingosine (Sph) and S1P (Merrill, 2002).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in sphingolipid biochemistry, supported by the cited reference.

claim: The SPT complex is composed of long chain subunit 1 (SPTLC1), subunit 2/3 (SPTLC2/3) and small subunit A/B (SPTSSA/B).
source: The SPT complex, which is composed of long chain subunit 1 (SPTLC1), subunit 2/3 (SPTLC2/3) and small subunit A/B (SPTSSA/B), catalyzes the rate-limiting step in the de novo SL biosynthetic pathway (Han et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in sphingolipid biochemistry, supported by the cited reference.

claim: The SPT complex catalyzes the rate-limiting step in the de novo SL biosynthetic pathway.
source: The SPT complex, which is composed of long chain subunit 1 (SPTLC1), subunit 2/3 (SPTLC2/3) and small subunit A/B (SPTSSA/B), catalyzes the rate-limiting step in the de novo SL biosynthetic pathway (Han et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in sphingolipid biochemistry, supported by the cited reference.

claim: Absence of any of the SPT subunits abolishes the enzymatic activity of SPT.
source: Absence of any of the subunits abolishes the enzymatic activity of SPT, which is required for normal embryonic development in mice (Hojjati et al., 2005).

claim: SPT enzymatic activity is required for normal embryonic development in mice.

claim: SPT enzyme activity is controlled by interaction with ORMDL proteins.
source: In addition, SPT enzyme activity is controlled by interaction with ORMDL proteins, which respond to extracellular and cell-intrinsic cues to regulate the flux of SL synthesis by the de novo pathway (Siow et al., 2015; Han et al., 2019).

claim: ORMDL proteins respond to extracellular and cell-intrinsic cues to regulate the flux of SL synthesis by the de novo pathway.

claim: Mutations in the SPTLC1 gene are associated with hereditary sensory neuropathy type 1 (HSAN1).
source: Mutations in the SPTLC1 gene are associated with peripheral neuronal dysfunction including hereditary sensory neuropathy type 1 (HSAN1) (Bejaoui et al., 2001; Dawkins et al., 2001), childhood amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) (Mohassel et al., 2021) and macular telengectasia type-2 (Gantner et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by the cited references.

claim: Mutations in the SPTLC1 gene are associated with childhood amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).
source: Mutations in the SPTLC1 gene are associated with peripheral neuronal dysfunction including hereditary sensory neuropathy type 1 (HSAN1) (Bejaoui et al., 2001; Dawkins et al., 2001), childhood amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) (Mohassel et al., 2021) and macular telengectasia type-2 (Gantner et al., 2019).

claim: Mutations in the SPTLC1 gene are associated with macular telengectasia type-2.

claim: Sptlc2 haploinsufficiency in macrophages causes reduction of circulating SM.
source: Sptlc2 haploinsufficiency in macrophages causes reduction of circulating SM and enhancement of reverse cholesterol transport in murine genetic models (Chakraborty et al., 2013), suggesting the requirement of this pathway in maintaining systemic SL homeostasis.

claim: Sptlc2 haploinsufficiency in macrophages causes enhancement of reverse cholesterol transport in murine genetic models.
source: Sptlc2 haploinsufficiency in macrophages causes reduction of circulating SM and enhancement of reverse cholesterol transport in murine genetic models (Chakraborty et al., 2013), suggesting the requirement of this pathway in maintaining systemic SL homeostasis.

claim: Loss of function of the SPT complex in hepatocytes reduces SM in the plasma membrane.
source: Loss of function of the SPT complex in hepatocytes reduces SM in the plasma membrane and suppresses the expression of E- and N-cadherin, adherens junction constituents (Li et al., 2016), highlighting the importance of this pathway in maintaining proper plasma membrane function.
evidence: This claim is supported by the cited reference.

claim: Loss of function of the SPT complex in hepatocytes suppresses the expression of E- and N-cadherin, adherens junction constituents.

claim: Endothelial cells (EC) line the inner layer of the circulatory system.
source: Endothelial cells (EC) line the inner layer of the circulatory system and mediate vascular tone control, barrier integrity, oxygen supply, immune cell trafficking and waste removal.

claim: Endothelial cells mediate vascular tone control, barrier integrity, oxygen supply, immune cell trafficking and waste removal.

claim: EC in CNS forms a specialized structure between the blood and the tissue, known as the blood brain barrier (BBB) and blood retinal barrier (BRB).
source: Indeed, EC in CNS forms a specialized structure between the blood and the tissue, known as the blood brain barrier (BBB) and blood retinal barrier (BRB) that consist of cellular compartments including EC, pericytes, and neural cells (astrocytes, glia and neurons).

claim: BBB and BRB consist of cellular compartments including EC, pericytes, and neural cells (astrocytes, glia and neurons).

claim: SL metabolites are critical for CNS development, physiology and disease.

claim: Metabolism of some lipids such as cholesterol are compartmentalized in CNS and non-CNS tissues.

claim: Sptlc1 ECKO mice exhibited delayed radial expansion of retinal vascular network at P6 compared to controls.

claim: Expression of CLDN5 was not altered in Sptlc1 ECKO retinal EC at P6.
source: However, expression of EC proteins important for BRB formation, including LEF1 (a key transcription factor involved in canonical Norrin/Wnt signaling), TFRC (transferrin receptor C), and CLDN5 (Claudin-5, a tight junction protein) were not altered at P6, suggesting that retinal EC organotypic specialization is not affected in the absence of SPT (Figure 3A–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-E.

claim: MFSD2A was upregulated in the retinal arteries of Sptlc1 ECKO retina.
source: Interestingly, MFSD2A, a lysophospholipid transporter that suppresses transcytosis in EC, was upregulated in the retinal arteries of Sptlc1 ECKO retina (Figure 3D and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and F.

claim: The delayed vascular developmental phenotype was normalized at P15.
source: The delayed vascular developmental phenotype was normalized at P15 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Vascular dropout was exacerbated at P10 and P12 in Sptlc1 ECKO mice in the OIR model.
source: In the absence of EC de novo SL synthesis, vascular dropout was exacerbated at P10 and P12, resulting in reduced vascular network density and increased avascular areas (Figure 4B–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B-G.

claim: Reduced SL de novo synthesis in EC led to reduced VEGF sensitivity of EC resulting in higher vascular dropout.
source: These results suggest that reduced SL de novo synthesis in EC led to reduced VEGF sensitivity of EC resulting in higher vascular dropout.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing increased vascular dropout in Sptlc1 ECKO mice in the OIR model.

claim: Pathological neovascularization was significantly attenuated in Sptlc1 ECKO mice at P17 in the OIR model.
source: With this timed gene deletion strategy, we observed significant attenuation of pathological neovascularization in Sptlc1 ECKO mice at P17 (Figure 4I and J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4I and J.

claim: Vaso-obliterated regions were larger in Sptlc1 ECKO mice at P17 in the OIR model.
source: In addition, vaso-obliterated regions were larger in Sptlc1 ECKO mice (Figure 4I and K).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4I and K.

claim: VEGF-treated capillaries in the vascular front were dilated with increased EC numbers 4 hr post-injection.
source: In concurrence with published reports (Eilken et al., 2017; Gerhardt et al., 2003), VEGF-treated capillaries in the vascular front were dilated with increased EC numbers as depicted by ERG staining 4 hr post-injection (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A-B and cited references.

claim: VEGF-induced capillary dilation and increased EC numbers were attenuated in Sptlc1 ECKO retinas.
source: These phenotypes were attenuated in Sptlc1 ECKO retinas, suggesting that VEGF responsiveness in EC is attenuated in the absence of de novo SL synthesis (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: The number of ESM1+ ectopic tip cells was reduced in Sptlc1 ECKO retinas compared to the Ctrl retinas after VEGF treatment.
source: Supporting our hypothesis, the number of ESM1+ ectopic tip cells was reduced in Sptlc1 ECKO retinas compared to the Ctrl retinas (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A-C.

claim: VEGF mediated ERK phosphorylation was attenuated by 72 hr of Myriocin pre-treatment in HUVEC.
source: In agreement with a previous report (Cantalupo et al., 2020), VEGF mediated ERK phosphorylation was attenuated by 72 hr of Myriocin pre-treatment (Figure 5D, lane 1–3).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and cited reference.

claim: 6 hr incubation of dhSph rescued ERK phosphorylation abrogated by Myriocin in HUVEC.
source: Importantly, 6 hr incubation of dhSph rescued ERK phosphorylation abrogated by Myriocin, suggesting that the de novo synthesis pathway of SL is required for efficient VEGF signaling (Figure 5D, lane 3–4).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Supplementation of Sph and Cer (C18:0) can restore VEGF-induced ERK phosphorylation from the inhibitory effects of Myriocin in HUVEC.
source: Supplementation of other SL including Sph and Cer (C18:0) can also restored VEGF-induced ERK phosphorylation from the inhibitory effects of Myriocin (Figure 5D, lane 3, 5, 6).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Myriocin treatment suppressed the CTXb signal at the plasma membrane in HUVEC.
source: In HUVEC, Myriocin treatment to inhibit SPT and SL synthesis suppressed the CTXb signal at the plasma membrane (Vascular Endothelial Cadherin (VECad) positive area) (Figure 5F left panels, quantified in G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F and G.

claim: Exogenous supplementation with dhSph and Sph for 6 hr rescued lipid rafts in the plasma membrane in Myriocin treated HUVEC.
source: In Myriocin treated cells, exogenous supplementation with dhSph and Sph for 6 hr rescued lipid rafts in the plasma membrane (Figure 5F right panels, quantified in G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5F and G.

claim: S1P levels were reduced ~60% in Sptlc1 ECKO plasma.
source: S1P and dhS1P levels were reduced ~60% in Sptlc1 ECKO (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: dhS1P levels were reduced ~60% in Sptlc1 ECKO plasma.
source: S1P and dhS1P levels were reduced ~60% in Sptlc1 ECKO (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The reduction of plasma S1P in Sptlc1 ECKO is more pronounced than that observed in sphingosine kinase-1 and –2 ECKO.
source: This reduction is more pronounced than that observed in sphingosine kinase-1 and –2 ECKO (Gazit et al., 2016) and S1P transporter (SPNS2) ECKO mice (Hisano et al., 2012; Mendoza et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison with cited references.

claim: The reduction of plasma S1P in Sptlc1 ECKO is more pronounced than that observed in S1P transporter (SPNS2) ECKO mice.
source: This reduction is more pronounced than that observed in sphingosine kinase-1 and –2 ECKO (Gazit et al., 2016) and S1P transporter (SPNS2) ECKO mice (Hisano et al., 2012; Mendoza et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison with cited references.

claim: dhSph was reduced significantly in Sptlc1 ECKO plasma.
source: dhSph, a sphingoid base synthesized in the de novo synthesis pathway, was also reduced significantly (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Cer species (C24:1, C24:0, C26:1, and C26:0) were reduced in Sptlc1 ECKO plasma.
source: Moreover, Cer species (C24:1, C24:0, C26:1, and C26:0) were reduced in Sptlc1 ECKO plasma, which resulted in reduction of total Cer in plasma (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B and C.

claim: Total Cer was reduced in Sptlc1 ECKO plasma.
source: Moreover, Cer species (C24:1, C24:0, C26:1, and C26:0) were reduced in Sptlc1 ECKO plasma, which resulted in reduction of total Cer in plasma (Figure 6B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: SM species were not altered in the plasma of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.
source: In contrast, SM species were not altered in the plasma of Sptlc1 ECKO mice (Figure 6D and E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6D and E.

claim: Sphingoid bases and their phosphorylated counterparts (dhSph, dhS1P, and S1P) were significantly reduced in Sptlc1 ECKO RBCs.
source: Sphingoid bases and their phosphorylated counterparts (dhSph, dhS1P, and S1P) were significantly reduced in Sptlc1 ECKO RBCs (Figure 6F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Cer species (C22:1, C22:0, C24:0, and C26:0) were reduced in Sptlc1 ECKO RBCs.
source: Cer species (C22:1, C22:0, C24:0, and C26:0) were also reduced (Figure 6G and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6G and H.

claim: SM species were not altered in RBC of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.
source: SM species were not altered in RBC of Sptlc1 ECKO mice (Figure 6I and J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6I and J.

claim: Rapid reduction of plasma S1P levels was observed as early as 1 week after tamoxifen-induced Sptlc1 deletion.
source: Rapid reduction of plasma S1P levels observed as early as 1 week and maintained thereafter (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Kinetics of RBC S1P reduction was similar to plasma S1P reduction after tamoxifen-induced Sptlc1 deletion.
source: Kinetics of RBC S1P reduction was similar (Figure 7B), suggesting that EC SL metabolites are rapidly secreted into plasma and that RBC and plasma SL pools are in rapid equilibrium under physiological conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: ApoM bound S1P was not affected in Sptlc1 ECKO plasma.
source: By fractionation of plasma using fast protein liquid chromatography, we determined that ApoM bound S1P was not affected while albumin bound S1P in the LPF was significantly reduced in Sptlc1 ECKO mice (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Albumin bound S1P in the LPF was significantly reduced in Sptlc1 ECKO mice.
source: By fractionation of plasma using fast protein liquid chromatography, we determined that ApoM bound S1P was not affected while albumin bound S1P in the LPF was significantly reduced in Sptlc1 ECKO mice (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Sphingoid bases and phosphorylated derivatives (dhSph, Sph, S1P, dhS1P) showed significant reduction from P14 to P28 in Sptlc1 ECKO mice with postnatal deletion.
source: Sphingoid bases and phosphorylated derivatives (dhSph, Sph, S1P, dhS1P) showed significant reduction from P14 to P28 in Sptlc1 ECKO mice (Figure 7D–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7D-G.

claim: Plasma dhCer, Cer and SM were not changed in Sptlc1 ECKO mice with postnatal deletion from P14 to P28.
source: In contrast, plasma dhCer, Cer and SM were not changed (Figure 7H–J, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7H-J and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: DhSph was significantly reduced in lung of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.
source: DhSph, a direct product of the de novo SL biosynthetic pathway was significantly reduced in lung and liver of Sptlc1 ECKO mice (Figure 8A and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A and D.

claim: DhSph was significantly reduced in liver of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.
source: DhSph, a direct product of the de novo SL biosynthetic pathway was significantly reduced in lung and liver of Sptlc1 ECKO mice (Figure 8A and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A and D.

claim: S1P and Sph levels in lung and liver were not reduced in Sptlc1 ECKO mice.
source: In contrast, S1P and Sph levels in these tissues were not reduced (Figure 8A and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A and D.

claim: Cer content was reduced about 30–50% in lung of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.
source: Cer content was reduced about 30–50% in both organs from Sptlc1 ECKO mice with C24:0 and C24:1 Cer species exhibiting largest changes (Figure 8B, C, E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B, C, E and F.

claim: Cer content was reduced about 30–50% in liver of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.
source: Cer content was reduced about 30–50% in both organs from Sptlc1 ECKO mice with C24:0 and C24:1 Cer species exhibiting largest changes (Figure 8B, C, E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B, C, E and F.

claim: C24:0 and C24:1 Cer species exhibited largest changes in lung and liver of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.
source: Cer content was reduced about 30–50% in both organs from Sptlc1 ECKO mice with C24:0 and C24:1 Cer species exhibiting largest changes (Figure 8B, C, E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8B, C, E and F.

claim: None of the SL metabolites were altered in retina by lack of EC SPT.
source: We also measured SL content of retina, a CNS organ system. In sharp contrast to lung and liver, none of the SL metabolites were altered by lack of EC SPT (Figure 8G–H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8G-H.

claim: SL metabolic flux from EC to adjacent tissues only occurs in circulation and non-CNS organs such as the lung and the liver but not in the retina.
source: These results reveal that the SL metabolic flux from EC to adjacent tissues only occurs in circulation and non-CNS organs such as the lung and the liver but not in the retina, which is part of the CNS.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing reduced SL metabolites in lung and liver but not retina of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: Liver function was normal in Sptlc1 ECKO mice.
source: Liver function was normal in Sptlc1 ECKO suggesting that reduced SL metabolites are not critical for hepatic homeostasis.
evidence: This claim is supported by the blood chemistry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: APAP treatment resulted in reduced liver injury in Sptlc1 ECKO mice compared with controls at early time points (4–8 hr).
source: APAP treatment resulted in reduced liver injury (aspartate aminotransferase (AST) levels and liver necrosis) in Sptlc1 ECKO mice compared with controls at early time points (4–8 hr) (Figure 9A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9A-C.

claim: Many SL metabolites (dhCer C16:0, dhSph, dhS1P, Sph, S1P, Cer C24:1, and total Cer) were lower in the liver at 8 hr post-APAP in Sptlc1 ECKO mice.
source: Many SL metabolites (dhCer C16:0, dhSph, dhS1P, Sph, S1P, Cer C24:1, and total Cer) were lower in the liver at 8 hr post-APAP but only dhCer C16:0 and dhSph were lower in the Sptlc1 ECKO mice at 24 hr (Figure 9D–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9D-I.

claim: Only dhCer C16:0 and dhSph were lower in the Sptlc1 ECKO liver at 24 hr post-APAP.
source: Many SL metabolites (dhCer C16:0, dhSph, dhS1P, Sph, S1P, Cer C24:1, and total Cer) were lower in the liver at 8 hr post-APAP but only dhCer C16:0 and dhSph were lower in the Sptlc1 ECKO mice at 24 hr (Figure 9D–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9D-I.

claim: Liver GSH levels were elevated in Sptlc1 ECKO mice prior to APAP injection.
source: Liver GSH levels were elevated in Sptlc1 ECKO mice prior to APAP injection. Even though GSH is diminished after APAP-administration, Sptlc1 ECKO mice still had higher GSH levels than the WT counterparts at 8 hr (Figure 9J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9J.

claim: Sptlc1 ECKO mice had higher GSH levels than the WT counterparts at 8 hr after APAP administration.
source: Liver GSH levels were elevated in Sptlc1 ECKO mice prior to APAP injection. Even though GSH is diminished after APAP-administration, Sptlc1 ECKO mice still had higher GSH levels than the WT counterparts at 8 hr (Figure 9J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 9J.

claim: Reduced flux of SL metabolites from EC to liver results in attenuated drug-induced hepatotoxicity via modulation of antioxidant GSH levels.
source: Thus, reduced flux of SL metabolites from EC to liver results in attenuated drug-induced hepatotoxicity via modulation of antioxidant GSH levels.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing reduced APAP-induced hepatotoxicity and elevated GSH levels in Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: De novo synthesis of SL in EC regulates developmental and pathological angiogenesis.
source: In this study, we show that SPT activity in EC regulates developmental and pathological angiogenesis.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing delayed retinal vascular development and reduced pathological neovascularization in Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: EC is a major SL source of circulatory SL species.
source: We also discover a novel function of EC as a major SL source of circulatory SL species, which determines the SL content of organs (the lung and the liver) and the response of liver hepatocytes to chemical injury.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing reduced SL metabolites in plasma, RBC, lung, and liver of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: EC-derived SL determines the SL content of organs (the lung and the liver).
source: We also discover a novel function of EC as a major SL source of circulatory SL species, which determines the SL content of organs (the lung and the liver) and the response of liver hepatocytes to chemical injury.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing reduced SL metabolites in lung and liver of Sptlc1 ECKO mice.

claim: EC-derived SL determines the response of liver hepatocytes to chemical injury.
source: We also discover a novel function of EC as a major SL source of circulatory SL species, which determines the SL content of organs (the lung and the liver) and the response of liver hepatocytes to chemical injury.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data showing reduced APAP-induced hepatotoxicity in Sptlc1 ECKO mice.
